Featured Project

Maori Learning CASE STUDY

Educational E-Commerce Platform

A complete UX/UI redesign of an education resource platform for South African learners, parents, tutors, and Educators.

UX/UI Design
Educational Platform
Wix
SEO

Before and After

Before
After

Maori Learning is an educational resource platform offering worksheets, printable resources, educational videos, songs, flipbooks, and learning materials for South African learners. The website serves homeschooling families, parents, tutors, and educators seeking engaging educational content aligned primarily with the CAPS curriculum.

The project involved redesigning an existing website that had grown organically over time and no longer met modern usability, mobile responsiveness, branding, or content organization standards.

  • My Role

    UX/UI Designer - Responsibilities included: Client discovery and requirements gathering UX audit of the existing website Information architecture planning User flow design Wireframing and layout planning Mobile responsiveness improvements Brand identity refinement Visual asset creation SEO optimization Content organization User dashboard planning Final implementation within Wix

  • Tools Used

    Figma (wireframing, brainstorming, planning, mockups) Wix (website design and implementation) ChatGPT (UX consultation, content strategy, SEO guidance) Emergent Labs (layout ideation and design exploration) AI Image Generation (custom illustrations, mascot poses, educational graphics)

  • Timeline

    Primary Build: Approximately 2 weeks Post-Handoff Revisions: Additional 2 days following client feedback for: Social media integration SEO improvements Search visibility optimization Final refinements

UX Audit

An audit of the existing website identified:
Navigation confusion
Product overload
Mobile layout issues
Missing legal documentation
Weak calls-to-action
Lack of content hierarchy

IA

The website structure was reorganized into:
Home
Shop
About
Videos & Songs
FAQ

Privacy Policy
Terms & Refund Policy

Wireframes

Low-fidelity wireframes were created in Figma to:
Plan content hierarchy
Test navigation structures
Explore homepage layouts
Evaluate dashboard concepts

Visual Design

A soft educational design language was created featuring:
Pastel gradients
Rounded interface elements
Educational iconography

Family-friendly visual hierarchy
Branding & Mascot Development

Branding

A key component of the redesign was expanding the Maori Learning owl mascot into a cohesive brand element.

Custom mascot variations were created including:
Flying owl / Reading owl / Teaching owl / Singing owl
Educational scene illustrations
The mascot became a recognizable visual anchor throughout the website.

Orginazation

Educational Resource Organization
Resources were restructured into clearer educational pathways including:
Foundation Phase
Intermediate Phase
Senior Phase
Further Education & Training

Custom visual category artwork was created for each phase to improve recognition and navigation.

Mobile responsiveness became one

of the project's largest areas of improvement.

Work included:

Touch-friendly interactions
Mobile readability improvements

SEO Strategy

SEO improvements included:
Custom page titles
Meta descriptions
Keyword planning
URL optimization

Educational content discoverability improvements
Post-launch revisions included additional keyword optimization to improve search visibility.

Final Outcome

The final solution delivered:
Complete visual redesign
Improved content organization
Enhanced educational branding
Responsive mobile experience

Educational video hub

SEO improvements

Results

The project concluded with successful client hand-off and positive client feedback.
Additional refinement requests were completed after launch, including social integration and SEO enhancements.
The client expressed satisfaction with both the redesign process and final outcome.

The original website suffered from several usability issues


Outdated visual design
Poor mobile responsiveness
Cluttered product listings
Weak information hierarchy
Limited trust-building elements
Confusing navigation structure
Inconsistent visual branding
Educational resources blended together without clear categorization
Lack of supporting legal and informational pages
The client also needed a solution that remained easy to maintain without requiring technical knowledge or complex workflows.

Key Challenges


Balancing Simplicity and Features
Many advanced features were explored but ultimately removed or simplified to ensure maintainability.
Educational Content Organization
Large numbers of educational products required clearer categorization and navigation.
Mobile ExperienceSignificant effort was invested in transforming the mobile experience into a modern and user-friendly interface.

Client requested: .
DISCOVERY & DECISION MAKING

Exploring the right solution

During discovery, several potential solutions were explored before simplifying the experience around what the client actually needed.

01

Original Direction

A subscription-based educational model was initially considered. After stakeholder discussions, it was removed due to the administrative complexity and ongoing maintenance it would require.

✕ Subscription Model
02

Concepts Explored

01 Membership-restricted content
02 Video lesson subscriptions
03 Advanced filtering systems
04 CMS-driven educational libraries
03

Final Direction

These ideas were ultimately simplified to create a solution that aligned more closely with the client's needs while remaining practical to manage and maintain long term.

✓ Simpler. More sustainable.
✦
KEY UX LESSON

The best solution isn't always the most technically advanced.

Sometimes the strongest UX decision is knowing what to leave out. By prioritising the client's actual needs over unnecessary complexity, the final experience became easier to use, manage, and maintain.

  • UX Strategy

    The redesign focused on four core principles

  • 1. Simplicity

    The client needed a website that remained easy to update and manage.

  • 2. Trust

    Parents must feel confident purchasing educational resources.

  • 3. Discoverability

    Users needed to find resources quickly based on grade and learning phase.

  • 4. Mobile Accessibility

    Many users access educational content from mobile devices.

Reflection

This project reinforced the importance of designing around real client needs rather than technical complexity.

Many initially ambitious features were simplified after evaluating long-term usability and maintainability. This experience strengthened my understanding of stakeholder communication, educational UX design, responsive web design, content organization, and balancing business goals with user needs.
Most importantly, the project demonstrated that effective UX often comes from reducing friction and simplifying systems rather than adding more features.
